fi-corydoras-panda.title: Panda Cory
fi-corydoras-panda.sci: Corydoras panda (now often listed as Hoplisoma panda)
fi-corydoras-panda.summary: A small, peaceful bottom-dweller with panda-like black patches. Happiest in a group and in slightly cool water.
rows: 18 × 12 in footprint (about 11 gal) or larger for a small group
Keep at least 6 together. They're shy and inactive alone
Omnivore. Sinking pellets or wafers as the staple, plus live or frozen daphnia, brine shrimp and bloodworm
72–77°F (22–25°C). Long-term warmer water shortens its life
Easy, but sensitive to dirty water and dirty substrate
Upper Amazon, Peru. Nearly all in the trade are farm-raised
notes: Use soft sand or smooth gravel and keep it clean. Corys can lose their whiskers (barbels) over dirty or rough substrate.
Avoid undergravel filters. Don't keep with large or aggressive fish.
warn: Likes cooler water (72–77°F). That doesn't overlap with heat-lovers like German blue rams (81–86°F).

fi-corydoras-aeneus.title: Bronze Corydoras
fi-corydoras-aeneus.summary: The bronze cory, Osteogaster aenea, long known as Corydoras aeneus, is an armoured catfish described from Trinidad and accepted to occur across much of South America. That range looks more like a…
rows: Type locality is 'Trinidad Island, West Indies', and it still occurs in some river systems of central and southern parts of the island.
notes: Ideally use a substrate of fine sand, although rounded gravel is an acceptable alternative provided it's kept scrupulously clean.
Other décor is largely down to personal choice, but some cover should be provided to give the fish security.

fi-corydoras-julii.title: Julii Corydoras
fi-corydoras-julii.summary: The julii cory, Hoplisoma julii, long known as Corydoras julii, is an armoured catfish from coastal river systems south of the Amazon delta in northeastern Brazil. Also known as 'leopard cory' or…
rows: Native to coastal river systems south of the Amazon delta in the states of Piauí, Maranhão, Pará, and Amapá, northeastern Brazil.
notes: Ideally use a substrate of fine sand, although rounded gravel is an acceptable alternative provided it is kept scrupulously clean.
Other décor is largely down to personal choice, but some cover should be provided to give the fish security.

fi-corydoras-melini.title: Melini Corydoras
fi-corydoras-melini.summary: The false bandit cory, Hoplisoma melini, long known as Corydoras melini, is an armoured catfish from tributaries of the rios Negro, Caquetá and Orinoco in Brazil and Colombia. Its oblique dark bar…
rows: Native to tributaries of the rios Negro , Caquetá (both within the Amazon basin), and Orinoco in northwestern Brazil and east-central Colombia.
notes: Ideally use a substrate of fine sand, although rounded gravel is an acceptable alternative provided it is kept scrupulously clean.
Other décor is largely down to personal choice, but some cover should be provided.

fi-corydoras-similis.title: Similis Corydoras
fi-corydoras-similis.summary: The smudge spot cory, Hoplisoma simile, long known as Corydoras similis, is an armoured catfish from the Rio Madeira basin in Brazil. Several species can be confused with it at first glance,…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Omnivore. Omnivorous and easy to feed.
Found in the Rio Madeira Basin, Brazil .
notes: Hoplisoma simile will thrive in a tank set up to replicate an Amazon biotope.

fi-corydoras-virginiae.title: Virginiae Corydoras
fi-corydoras-virginiae.summary: The Miguelito cory, Brochis virginiae, long known as Corydoras virginiae, is an armoured catfish considered endemic to the río Ucayali drainage in Peru. It is sometimes referred to as 'Virginia's…
rows: Type locality is the río Ucayali , Peru , and this species is considered endemic to that drainage.
notes: Ideally use a substrate of fine sand, although rounded gravel is an acceptable alternative provided it's kept scrupulously clean.
Other décor is largely down to personal choice, but some cover should be provided to give the fish security.

fi-corydoras-paleatus.title: Corydoras paleatus
fi-corydoras-paleatus.summary: The pepper cory, Hoplisoma paleatum, long known as Corydoras paleatus, is an armoured catfish from southern Brazil, Uruguay, Paraguay and Argentina. Along with the bronze cory it is one of the most…
rows: Omnivore. Gut analyses of wild specimens have shown it to be an opportunistic omnivore , consuming a range of worms, crustaceans , plant matter and other zoobenthos .
Native to parts of southern Brazil , Uruguay , Paraguay and Argentina .
notes: Corydoras species prefer sandy substrate as they enjoy rooting about in it looking for morsels of food.
Can be prone to infection of the barbels if kept in poorly maintained gravel.

fi-corydoras-sterbai.title: Corydoras sterbai
fi-corydoras-sterbai.summary: Sterba's cory, Hoplisoma sterbai, long known as Corydoras sterbai, is a peaceful armoured catfish from Bolivia and Brazil, marked with light spots on a dark head. Almost all fish in the trade are…
rows: Schooling / social — keep a proper group
Omnivore. Omnivorous and easy to feed.
notes: Hoplisoma sterbai will thrive in a tank set up to replicate an Amazon biotope.

fi-corydoras-adolfoi.title: Adolfoi Corydoras
fi-corydoras-adolfoi.summary: Adolfo's cory, Hoplisoma adolfoi, long known as Corydoras adolfoi, is an armoured catfish apparently highly endemic to the upper rio Negro near São Gabriel da Cachoeira, Brazil. One of several rio…
rows: Type locality is given as 'Small tributary of the upper Rio Negro on the equator near São Gabriel da Cachoeira, Brazil ', and this species is apparently highly endemic there.
notes: Ideally use a substrate of fine sand, although rounded gravel is an acceptable alternative provided it's kept scrupulously clean.
Other décor is largely down to personal choice, but some cover should be provided to give the fish security.

fi-corydoras-agassizi.title: Agassizi Corydoras
fi-corydoras-agassizi.summary: The spotted cory, Brochis agassizii, long known as Corydoras agassizii, is an armoured catfish from the Amazon around the border of Brazil and Peru, described from near Tabatinga. Its name is…
rows: Type locality is ' Amazon River near Tabatinga, Amazonas, Brazil '.
notes: Ideally use a substrate of fine sand, although rounded gravel is an acceptable alternative provided it's kept scrupulously clean.
Other décor is largely down to personal choice, but some cover should be provided to give the fish security.

fi-corydoras-duplicareus.title: Duplicareus Corydoras
fi-corydoras-duplicareus.summary: Hoplisoma duplicareum, long known as Corydoras duplicareus, is an armoured catfish known only from a small portion of the upper rio Negro system in Brazil. It belongs to a group of rio Negro…
rows: Known only from a small portion of the upper rio Negro system in Brazil .
notes: Ideally use a substrate of fine sand, although rounded gravel is an acceptable alternative provided it’s kept scrupulously clean.
Other décor is largely down to personal choice, but some cover should be provided to give the fish security.

fi-corydoras-elegans.title: Elegans Corydoras
fi-corydoras-elegans.summary: The elegant cory, Gastrodermus elegans, long known as Corydoras elegans, is an armoured catfish from the western Amazon basin in Peru, Ecuador and Brazil. Unlike most congeners it spends a fair…
rows: This species is fairly widespread in the western Amazon basin and has been recorded in the Ríos Yavarí (Javary), Itaya , Nanay , Carahuayte , Tamaya , Ampiyacu , and Ucayali in…
notes: Ideally use a substrate of fine sand, although rounded gravel is an acceptable alternative provided it’s kept scrupulously clean.
Other décor is largely down to personal choice, but some cover should be provided to give the fish security.

fi-corydoras-splendens.title: Emerald Green Corydoras
fi-corydoras-splendens.summary: The emerald 'brochis', Brochis splendens, long known as Corydoras splendens, is an armoured catfish recorded throughout much of the Amazon basin in Brazil, Peru, Ecuador and Colombia. It is sometimes…
rows: This species is one of the more widespread than other members of the genus and has been recorded throughout much of the Amazon basin in Brazil , Peru , Ecuador and Colombia .
notes: Ideally use a substrate of fine sand, although rounded gravel is an acceptable alternative provided it is kept scrupulously clean.
Other décor is largely down to personal choice, but some cover should be provided to give the fish security.
